result:
Solution 1 is the most likely correct answer, though I can't fully verify the sharp constant for every p from memory.

**Why Solutions 2 and 3 fail.** Both give β(p) = max(1, 1/(p−1)) with no extra term. Their lower bound comes only from scalar weights W = wI, which the problem's [W]_{A_p} reduces to the classical A_p characteristic. That lower bound is valid but not sharp for genuinely matrix-valued weights. For p = 2, the Domelevo–Petermichl–Treil–Volberg result ("The matrix A₂ conjecture fails, i.e. 3/2 > 1") shows the sharp exponent is 3/2, not 1. The bound [W]_{A₂}^{3/2} is also the known upper bound from Nazarov–Petermichl–Treil–Volberg. Solutions 2 and 3 therefore understate β(2), and their formulas are inconsistent with the p = 2 limit of the true answer. Solution 2 also contains a duality step that does not check out.

**Why Solution 1 fits.** Solution 1 keeps the scalar lower bound max(1, 1/(p−1)) and adds the matrix-specific extra 1/2. This gives 3/2 at p = 2, consistent with the known matrix A₂ result, and reproduces the scalar exponent when shifted by the matrix correction. The formula β(p) = max(1, 1/(p−1)) + 1/2 is the form I recall from the sharp matrix-weighted theory for p ≠ 2. I have not re-derived the lower-bound construction for general p, so this rests on recall of the literature rather than a full check.

CHOICE: 1
